label: D2 after choosing a1 and landing in S2 (a1 rare transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2, exactly when the last-action input is a1 and the shown state is S2, i.e. the rare transition after choosing a1 (dev P=1.00, R=1.00). The predicate uses only inputs the agent sees at D2, so no future variables are needed. Equivalent to action==1 & state==2 at D2. It never fires at D1 or GO, on a1->S1 (common), or on any a2 trial, including a2->S1 rare. Magnitude is nearly constant (median 4.64, max 5.24). In the top windows the strongest activations came on a1->S2 trials whose D1 showed no reward, but I only saw this in examples and did not check it systematically. The feature is the conjunction of the a1 choice and the S2 state, not a general rare-transition detector.

issues: None of my checks broke the claim. Predicate (phase==D2)&(in_action==1)&(in_state==2): dev P=1.000, R=0.99998, F1=0.99999 (45685 of 45686 active steps). Test P=R=F1=mass recall=1.000 (46977 steps). The version using action/state instead of in_action/in_state gives the same scores.

The misses run on dev found 0 false positives and 1 missed activation. That one step is a D2 on a1->S1 (common) with activation of about 0.00 relative to the max, which is noise. On test there are no misses and no false positives.

The profile confirms the stated facts. Activation is 0 at D1 and GO (100% of mass at D2). There is 0 activation when in_action is 2. There is 1 negligible step at in_state==1, and none on common transitions apart from that same step. So the feature is the a1 and S2 conjunction, not a general rare-transition detector.

The hedged magnitude claim (strongest when the D1 showed no reward) is mildly supported, though not strongly. On test, the share of active steps covered by the prev_reward==0 split rises with activation quartile (0.26, 0.29, 0.37, 0.44). The prev_reward==1 split falls (0.74, 0.71, 0.63, 0.56). Magnitude is nearly constant (median 4.64, max 5.24), so this is only a small modulation.
The core trial's D2 has a higher firing rate (0.224 vs about 0.09 at other window positions). This follows from how the windows were sampled, not from the feature itself.
No future variables are needed: in_action and in_state are both observed at D2.
